response.consequence: One failing or missing row stops processing of all later unscheduled reminders in that cron run, and the endpoint returns a 500. If the success-path DB update failed after Twilio accepted the SMS, retryCount is bumped (when the DB is reachable) and the SMS is rescheduled on the next run, which sends a duplicate.
response.explanation: The new catch block calls prisma.workflowReminder.update to bump retryCount, and that call is not wrapped in its own try/catch. If it throws, the exception escapes the per-reminder loop. For example, the row may have been deleted concurrently, or the DB call may fail. The same update can also throw because the earlier success-path update (scheduled: true) failed after twilio.scheduleSMS had already succeeded. In that case the catch re-throws from the DB, and the SMS was already scheduled at Twilio. The handler then rejects instead of continuing to the remaining reminders.
response.title: Unguarded retryCount update inside catch block can abort the whole cron run

response.consequence: Permanently unschedulable SMS reminders are re-evaluated on every cron run until their scheduledDate passes. Each run repeats the profile lookup and template rendering for them, and the retry cap does not bound that work. The impact is limited because scheduledDate eventually deletes the rows.
response.explanation: The new retry logic increments retryCount only when twilio.scheduleSMS returns a falsy value or throws. The guard `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` has no else branch. A reminder whose message resolves to empty (for example, no reminderBody and a non-REMINDER template) or whose sendTo is missing (no smsReminderNumber on the booking) is neither scheduled nor counted as a failure. It stays `scheduled: false` and the cron selects it again on every run. The `retryCount > 1` cleanup added to deleteMany never applies to these rows, so only the scheduledDate cleanup removes them. In addition, the new `retryCount > 1` clause in the delete's OR is not restricted to `method: SMS`. Only the SMS cron uses the column today, so this is currently latent.
response.title: Reminders with empty message or missing sendTo never increment retryCount

response.explanation: The migration adds "retryCount" INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, and schema.prisma declares retryCount Int @default(0). Type, nullability and default match. On Postgres 11 and later, adding a column with a constant default is a metadata-only change and does not rewrite the table. Deploy ordering (migration before code) is the standard Prisma flow, and nothing in the supplied snapshot shows otherwise.

response.consequence: With overlapping cron invocations, failing reminders can take more retries than intended to pass the `retryCount > 1` cleanup threshold. Duplicate SMS can also be scheduled for the same reminder. Both effects are limited to cron overlap.
response.explanation: The handler reads reminders with findMany and later writes `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`. This happens in the `else` branch (line 184) and again in the `catch` block (line 195). Both writes use the value read at the start of the run, not `{ increment: 1 }`. Both updates are keyed only on `id`, with no `scheduled: false` condition. If two cron runs overlap, both read the same retryCount and both write N+1, so one failure is lost. Both runs also pick up the same unscheduled reminder, so both can call twilio.scheduleSMS for it. Each run then sets scheduled=true with its own sid, so the user gets a duplicate SMS. The first run's reference is overwritten, so it can no longer be cancelled.

other_findings.consequence: One bad row can block SMS scheduling for the rest of the batch. A transient DB error after a successful Twilio schedule can produce duplicate SMS.
other_findings.explanation: The new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the catch block (lines 190-198) is not itself guarded. If the reminder row was deleted concurrently, or the DB errors, the update throws out of the handler. The remaining reminders are then skipped and the request returns a 500. Separately, the `scheduled: true` update at about lines 170-177 sits inside the same try. If that update fails after twilio.scheduleSMS succeeded, the catch increments retryCount and the reminder stays scheduled=false. The next run schedules the SMS again.
